note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: From human uncertainty lookup table to LLM-specific VOCAL and its results

nodes.name: Existing UQ is costly or unnatural
nodes.description: Logits-based UQ suffers from lexical sensitivity and overhead, sampling-based UQ is slow and costly, and numeric verbal confidence is unnatural compared with qualitative markers like 'likely'.

nodes.name: UM-Lookup built from literature and annotators
nodes.description: The UM-Lookup maps 115 distinct verbal uncertainty markers to numeric values, built from psychology and decision-science literature, debiased, and aggregated over judgments from more than 300 human annotators.

nodes.name: Multiple markers are averaged
nodes.description: When a response contains several uncertainty markers, they are averaged into one score (humans average multiple verbal probability terms), giving q = mean(1 - UM-Lookup(u_i)).

nodes.name: Human lookup gives non-trivial UQ
nodes.description: The human-sourced lookup quantifier Q_VU-H achieves AUROC significantly above 0.5 in 7 of 8 model-dataset configurations; with GPT-4o on SciQ it beats PE and SE by 4.7% and 5.6% AUROC.

nodes.name: Human lookup is unreliable
nodes.description: Q_VU-H is frequently outperformed by PE and can fail, e.g. AUROC falls below chance for GPT-4o on GSM8K (about 0.41), because a human score for a marker does not always match the LLM's internal uncertainty.

nodes.name: LLMs interpret markers differently from humans
nodes.description: GPT-4o assigns 0.677 confidence to 'almost certain' (humans 0.92) and 0.355 to 'very likely' (humans 0.853), so human-derived tables do not transfer directly to LLMs.

nodes.name: VOCAL learns marker scores from LLM outputs
nodes.description: VOCAL learns a numerical score per uncertainty marker by minimizing a binary cross-entropy loss between the aggregated marker uncertainty of a generation and its correctness, a convex problem under logistic loss.

nodes.name: Laplacian smoothing handles sparse markers
nodes.description: Because rare markers have unstable learned values, VOCAL applies graph Laplacian regularization over a marker similarity graph so semantically similar markers get similar scores.

nodes.name: VOCAL beats human lookup
nodes.description: VOCAL consistently improves AUROC over Q_VU-H across models and datasets, e.g. raising GPT-4o on GSM8K from 0.41 to around 0.6.

nodes.name: VOCAL beats single-sample UQ
nodes.description: VOCAL achieves the highest AUROC in 5 of 6 settings against single-sample baselines G-NLL and PPL; on GSM-Hard with DeepSeek-V3.1 it reaches 0.715 versus 0.520 (G-NLL) and 0.567 (PPL).

nodes.name: VOCAL competitive with multi-sample UQ
nodes.description: Using one response, VOCAL is competitive with multi-sample UQ baselines (best on SciQ with Qwen2.5-72B, AUROC 0.717), though multi-sample metrics sometimes surpass it on TriviaQA.

nodes.name: Calibration improves post hoc
nodes.description: VOCAL has average vanilla ECE 0.1314, near the best baseline; with isotonic regression it reaches the best average ECE of 0.0281.

nodes.name: More training data helps
nodes.description: Increasing VOCAL training samples from 100 to 500 raises AUROC from about 0.52 to 0.60.

nodes.name: Learned scores partly transfer across LLMs
nodes.description: Training and testing VOCAL on different LLMs' SciQ responses yields AUROC of 0.60-0.72, indicating shared structure but model-specific differences.

isolated_nodes.name: Advanced LLMs express diverse markers
isolated_nodes.description: Advanced LLMs like GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3.1 express more diverse uncertainty markers than small models like Llama-3.1-8B, which tend to be overconfident.

isolated_nodes.name: Verbal uncertainty prompting is harmless
isolated_nodes.description: Eliciting verbal uncertainty does not impose a significant performance penalty on the models' problem-solving.

isolated_nodes.name: Wide model and dataset evaluation
isolated_nodes.description: Experiments evaluate GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3.1 on GSM-Hard, GSM8K, MedQA and PIQA with five-shot CoT prompting.

structural_reasoning: Human lookup baseline and its failure motivate VOCAL, whose design leads to the empirical results; peripheral observations are isolated.
